title: Turn-boundary-aware slot harmonizer and soft-KV compaction tuning for mixed-turn latency stability
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: In production traces for chat-style workloads we observe intermittent 95th/99th token latency spikes when a long prompt is followed by many short responses (and vice versa). These spikes correlate with slot fragmentation at turn boundaries and aggressive KV residency churn when the scheduler immediately packs differing-length turns into existing slots.

Goal: Reduce tail token-latency variance for mixed prompt/response workloads without increasing average per-token cost or degrading throughput. Approach is to tune the slot harmonizer to be turn-boundary-aware and to introduce a soft-KV compaction policy that reduces unnecessary KV eviction during transient length shifts.

Hypothesis: If the scheduler biases coalescing to preserve turn contiguity for a short time-window (turn-boundary grace), and KV compaction is delayed with a conservative shrink-first policy, then tail latencies will fall by >20% on 95th/99th while avg token throughput stays within 5% of baseline.

Constraints: Must not require model changes. Changes must be configurable via scheduler knobs and exposed in staging console. Must maintain existing SLA on throughput within Dedicated pools.

Success criteria and how measured are in acceptance_criteria.
acceptance_criteria: 95th token latency reduced by >=20% on mixed-turn benchmark compared to baseline run (same traffic profile)
99th token latency reduced by >=15% on same benchmark
Average tokens/s throughput change <= 5% compared to baseline
GPU memory fragmentation metric (slot_fragmentation_ratio) decreases by >=10%
No increase in KV miss rate > 3% from baseline (measured per 10k requests)
Config knobs added to runtime to tune: turn_boundary_grace_ms, slot_stickiness, kv_soft_compact_threshold, kv_compact_cooldown_ms
E2E canary run on Dedicated pool (staging) with 1-hour ramp and automated rollback on regressions
Design doc and perf dashboard links added to ticket and reviewed by PM and SRE
tasks: Implement turn_boundary_grace window in continuous-batcher coalescer (scheduler change)
Add slot_stickiness weight to prefer existing slot if last request from same conversation within grace window
Introduce kv_soft_compact_threshold policy: prefer left-shift compaction (merge adjacent small KV regions) and avoid full eviction under transient pressure
Expose four scheduler knobs in runtime config + console UI toggles
Run controlled microbenchmarks with synthetic mixed-turn traces and collect metrics (tail latencies, throughput, kv miss rate, slot fragmentation)
Prepare canary pipeline config for Dedicated staging and implement automatic rollback criteria
Iterate on thresholds based on benchmark results and PM/SRE feedback
Document changes in design doc and update Runtime API changelog
decisions: Do a conservative rollout: stage -> canary (10% capacity) -> 50% -> full. Rollback triggers are defined in acceptance_criteria
Prefer parameterized knobs over hard-coded heuristics to allow per-customer tuning on Dedicated
KV compaction uses a soft-first approach (merge/shift vs immediate eviction) to reduce cold-KV churn
No change to model serving kernels or batch size heuristics in this ticket to limit blast radius
benchmark_results: Baseline run (2026-02-18): mixed-turn synthetic trace: P50=12ms P95=142ms P99=310ms tokens/s=48.3 slot_fragmentation_ratio=0.39 kv_miss_rate=0.021
Initial experiment (w/ turn_boundary_grace=40ms, slot_stickiness=0.6, kv_soft_compact_threshold=0.75): P50=12ms P95=108ms P99=258ms tokens/s=47.9 slot_fragmentation_ratio=0.31 kv_miss_rate=0.023
Trade-off observed: small uplift in kv_miss_rate (+0.2%) but meaningful tail improvement; throughput drop within 1%
Further tuning candidate (grace=25ms, stickiness=0.45) looks promising in small-scale tests: P95=116ms P99=268ms tokens/s=48.1
